title: Palindrome Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return `true` if the sequence of node values reads the same forward and backward (i.e., forms a palindrome), or `false` otherwise.

Try to solve the problem in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^5].
hints: Copying all node values into an array and using two pointers works in O(n) time and O(n) space.
To achieve O(1) extra space, use slow and fast pointers to find the midpoint of the list.
Reverse the second half in-place, compare the two halves node by node, and optionally reverse the second half back to restore the list.

examples.explanation: 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 reads the same forward and backward.
1 -> 2 reversed is 2 -> 1, which differs from the original list.
1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 is an odd-length palindrome centered at 3.
